The CED says 'a plot of the natural log (ln) of the reactant concentration as a function of time will be linear' for first order (5.3.A.2), and 'a plot of the reciprocal of the concentration of that reactant versus time will be linear' for second order (5.3.A.3). A mnemonic for this required list is admissible, and its caution calls for naming the plot and order explicitly, but the incorrect cue mappings make the hook unacceptable.

entry.reasons: a_factual: CED 5.3.A.2 says 'a plot of the natural log (ln) of the reactant concentration as a function of time will be linear' for first order, and 5.3.A.3 says 'a plot of the reciprocal of the concentration... versus time will be linear' for second order. The zeroth-order equation in 5.3.A.4 ([A]t − [A]0 = −kt) makes [A] versus t linear. The items list the three orders in the correct sequence and the correct plots. b_topic_codes: 5.3 is the topic whose Learning Objective 5.3.A ('Identify the rate law expression... using data that show how the concentrations... change over time') first requires this, and it is the only topic code listed. c_ced_required: 5.3.A.1 ('The order of a reaction can be inferred from a graph of concentration of reactant versus time') and 5.3.A.2–5.3.A.4 require students to identify order from these plots. d_caution: the entry's wording ('ln[A] versus t is linear') is equivalent to the CED's phrasing, so no caution is strictly required. The null caution is acceptable.

hooks.reasons: e_expansion: the cues are mismapped. 'flip' is expanded to 'first order: 1/[A] versus t is linear', but the CED (5.3.A.2, 5.3.A.3) gives 1/[A] versus t for SECOND order and ln[A] versus t for FIRST order. 'log' is expanded to 'second order: ln[A] versus t is linear', which is the reverse of the CED. Plain (zeroth, [A] vs t) is correct, but the expansion is not in the correct order or with the correct members. f_admissible: a mnemonic recalling the three-order sequence is the right kind of hook, and its caution ('name the plot and the order explicitly') matches the exam-wording point, but the hook as built encodes the wrong plot-to-order associations for first and second order, so it would teach students incorrect content the CED requires them to get right.

entry.reasons: a_factual: The body matches 5.3.A.1 ('The order of a reaction can be inferred from a graph of concentration of reactant versus time'). The three items match 5.3.A.2-5.3.A.3 and the integrated forms: zeroth order is [A]t - [A]0 = -kt (linear in [A] vs t), first order is ln[A]t - ln[A]0 = -kt (linear in ln[A] vs t), and second order is 1/[A]t - 1/[A]0 = kt (linear in 1/[A] vs t). The order and membership are correct. b_topic_codes: 5.3 is where integrated rate-law plots first appear, and the entry's only topic code is 5.3. c_ced_required: LO 5.3.A ('Identify the rate law expression of a chemical reaction using data that show how the concentrations of reaction species change over time') requires exactly this plot-to-order identification. d_caution: The entry's wording is essentially the CED's ('linear', 'reciprocal of the concentration', 'natural log'), so no caution is strictly required. The entry is accepted.

hooks.reasons: e_expansion: The cue-to-order mapping is wrong for two of three cues. 'flip' is mapped to 'first order: 1/[A] versus t is linear', but 1/[A] versus t is linear for second order (CED 5.3.A.3). 'log' is mapped to 'second order: ln[A] versus t is linear', but ln[A] versus t is linear for first order (CED 5.3.A.2). Only 'Plain' (zeroth order, [A] versus t, CED 5.3.A.4 equation) is correct. The expansions are also out of step with the entry's own items, which assign first order to ln and second order to 1/[A]. f_admissible: The hook is meant to recall the plot-to-order list, which the CED requires. As written, though, it recalls an incorrect mapping that would lead students to name the wrong order on the exam, so it is not admissible. Its caution about naming the plot and order explicitly does not fix the swapped expansions.
